findings.title: The mix runs over full scale: the functional cues together, and a crash that brings a Snap
findings.evidence: I recorded what the mixer really puts out (the Audio autoload driven with snapshots under --write-movie, 48 kHz; probes /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/rev4/rec_probe2.gd and rec_probe4.gd) and counted samples at full scale. (a) The car on the rumble strip with the indicator on, engine at 100 km/h, radio on music: 8 samples at full scale in 2.9 s; with a long yawn on top, 111 samples in 18 runs (the longest 12 samples) in 3.9 s. The same scene with the Master bus at -12 dB shows the real peaks: 1.017 and 1.379 of full scale (+2.8 dBFS). The cues play on the Cues bus, which nothing turns down, at -3, -2 and -8 dB from buffers normalised to 0.9: peaks of 0.64, 0.72 and 0.36. (b) With no cue sounding: a crash that brings a Snap during Pound, on a Patrol with music: 20 samples at full scale over six crashes; real peak up to 1.152, over full scale in 3 of the 6. There is no limiter (the builder's decision), and the audio check does not look: with indicator_tick at gain_db +6 it still prints '1035 checks, 0 failure(s)'. GDD 16.5: the cues 'must be audible over everything else'. They are, but they distort when two of them meet, and a yawn followed by the rumble strip is the game's own loop (GDD 2.4, 5.8).
findings.fix: Data only: take 5 dB off every gain_db in data/sfx.json (33 numbers) and leave the duck depths as they are. Cues and the rest fall together, so the check's margins do not move: tried in a scratch copy with 4 dB off all 33, the audio check printed the same 6.1, 6.1, 6.5 and 6.5 dB and 1035 checks, 0 failures. The mix is linear, so with 5 dB off the two measured peaks become 0.78 and 0.65 of full scale. (Also recorded: the four cues 4 dB down with their ducks 4 dB deeper peak at 0.74 with no sample at full scale.) Then let _check_mix in tools/audio_check.gd add up the peaks of rumble_strip, indicator_tick and one yawn (peak times 10^(gain_db/20): 0.96 after the change) and fail above 1.

findings.title: The Rattle fault can be neither seen nor heard
findings.evidence: GDD 16.3, first row: 'Lamps and faults: Five dashboard lamps, plus each fault's visible or audible effect'. Rattle (data/faults.json: nerves_per_s 0.2) is the one fault with nothing to see: the cabin view lights a count of identical lamps (src/view/cabin_view.gd 181 to 185), and 'rattle' occurs nowhere under src/view or src/game but in a comment of stop_view.gd, on this branch, on the tip d8c77a4 and in the two other parked M10 patches. sfx.json has no rattle, and Audio.apply never reads snapshot["faults"], which carries the ids of the active faults (DriveSim.FAULT_RATTLE). So +0.2 Nerves a second arrive with nothing to tell the player what causes them. Neither report mentions it; the engineer read the piece against 16.3 and 'found nothing to change'.
findings.fix: A looped 'rattle' entry in data/sfx.json (noise in short bursts, quiet, on the Bed bus) and three lines in Audio.apply: wanted while snapshot["faults"] holds DriveSim.FAULT_RATTLE, the car moves and it is not wrecked; a check beside _check_rumble. The table of GDD 16.5 has no such sound, so this is a decision under GDD 1.5 like horn_behind; nothing under src/core is needed.

findings.title: A jump in Suspicion or in Nerves is heard one old gap late
findings.evidence: Audio._set_pulse (line 747) stores the new gap, but the countdown to the next sound keeps the gap that held at the last one. Probe through Audio.apply at 60 frames a second (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/rev4/lag_probe.gd): watched at Suspicion 0 (a chirp at 0.00 s), Suspicion 100 from 0.50 s on: the next chirps come at 3.00, 3.80 and 4.60 s, the first 2.5 s after the jump where the data say every 0.8 s. Heartbeat: Pound at Nerves 80 (a beat at 0.00 s), Nerves 100 from 0.20 s on: beats at 1.00, 1.50 s. The same showed in the recording of the real mixer. GDD 16.3 gives Suspicion one sound, the siren's chirps; the jumps of GDD 6.5 (+30 for the phone, +40 for contraband) are what the player most needs to hear at once.
findings.fix: One line in _set_pulse, before the early return for a pulse that stays on: pulse.left = minf(pulse.left, every). Tried in a scratch copy: the same probe gives chirps at 0.00, 1.30, 2.10 s and beats at 0.00, 0.70, 1.20 s, and the audio check still prints 1035 checks, 0 failures.

findings.title: Fifth gear's added harmonic can come out weaker than none
findings.evidence: engine_harmonic is a second, free-running player tuned to harmonics 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 of the engine's pitch. The 24-harmonic saw already has all of these (its 2nd at half the strength of its fundamental), so the two add by whatever phase the last gear change or restart left. Recorded through the real mixer over 18 two-second stretches of gear changes (rec_probe3.gd in the same scratch folder): in fifth gear at 160 km/h the 360 Hz line stood at -22.3, -23.9, -22.7, -25.5, -25.8 and -31.8 dB, where the saw alone has -30.0 dB: in the last stretch the 'added' harmonic left it 1.8 dB weaker than nothing added. Third gear: -28.3 and -25.6 dB. GDD 16.5: 'a different added harmonic per gear'; GDD 16.3: gear is read from the engine's pitch.
findings.fix: Data only: "per_gear": [0, 12, 11, 10, 9, 8] in engine_harmonic (shifting up still drops the note). The saw's own harmonics there lie 18 to 22 dB under its fundamental. The same recording with these numbers: the added harmonic stands 14.9 to 18.8 dB over the saw's own in every stretch (-25.5 to -28.2 dB), and the audio check passes unchanged (1035 checks, 0 failures).

findings.title: Through the Wreck cut the frozen snapshot keeps ringing, chirping, beating and honking
findings.evidence: DriveSim.step returns early for the 3 s of a Wreck in a Telling, so the snapshot stands still and Audio.apply goes on repeating what it says. A whole Telling in the real scene (--table=drivers --seed=3 --bot=line, 90,000 frames, I99_AUDIO_LOG): crash and Wreck at frame 68430, 'engine ends' at 68465, then phone_ring at 68457 and 68541 and six heartbeats (68430 to 68594) before the retelling at 68610. A probe with a scrape that is both the fifth lamp and the Snap (wreck_probe.gd in the same scratch folder): the cut lasted 3.00 s, the snapshot said snap for all of it, and the horn sounded for 3.00 s (GDD 6.1 gives a Snap 2 s). Only the engine and the rumble strip heed `wrecked` (audio.gd 275 and 283); by the same code a Patrol's siren and the indicator go on too. GDD 3.2: at a Wreck 'the screen cuts to black one frame before impact' and a guest objects.
findings.fix: In Audio.apply, 'and not wrecked' in the conditions of the horn, horn_behind, the hum and the four pulses (lines 287 to 326), as the engine and the rumble strip have it. Tried in a scratch copy: the horn then lasts 0.43 s into the cut (the honk the simulation asked for), and the audio check still prints 1035 checks, 0 failures. Whether the radio plays on over the cut is the owner's to say.

findings.title: Play keys that mean nothing for a sound are accepted in silence
findings.evidence: The piece's own rule (commit d7932ec and the decisions of both reports): 'a key nothing reads, or one that means nothing for that sound, is an error at boot'. That holds for the generator's keys (SfxSynth._idle_keys), not for Audio's. In a scratch copy I gave `crash`, a one-shot that is no cue and no pulse, "every": 2, "duck_db": -10, "hold": 1.0, "fade_in": 0.5, "per_gear": [1, 2] and "speed_hz": [1, 2]: boot.tscn printed data_errors=0 and no error line, validate_data 0 errors, the audio check '1041 checks, 0 failure(s)'. Audio._make_voice (line 474) and _check_entries in tools/audio_drive_check.gd only ask that a key is in PLAY_KEYS. A duck_db without "functional", or an "every" on a sound that does not repeat, is 'a number that silently does nothing', which is what the check's own comment says it is there to prevent.
findings.fix: In Audio._make_voice add a problem for duck_db, duck_attack or duck_release without "functional" and for fade_in, fade_out or hold without "loop"; in _configure, for every, per_minute, speed_kmh, speed_hz, idle_hz, per_gear and warble on any sound but the one that reads them (a small table of key and ids).

findings.title: The audio check fails when another checkout's run clears user://test_runs
findings.evidence: _check_stream_files (line 599) writes user://test_runs/tool/audio_check_stream.wav. Every copy of the project shares that folder, and tests/run_tests.gd:58, tests/test_data.gd:655 and tools/smoke_all.gd:55 delete user://test_runs as they finish. I ran the audio check while a second process cleared the folder: 'ERROR: Condition "file.is_null()" is true', 'AUDIO FAIL stream: cannot write user://test_runs/tool/audio_check_stream.wav to try it', exit 1. In tools/check.sh that is a CHECK FAILED which says nothing about the sound, and checks do run side by side here (the engineer got round it by setting XDG_DATA_HOME). Game.write_save guards the same case (src/game/game.gd line 89: 'The folder may have been cleared away since the game started'). Otherwise the check is steady: 24 runs, each with a data folder of its own, eight at a time on four cores, all passed.
findings.fix: In _check_stream_files, DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(Game.user_dir)) just before save_to_wav, as Game.write_save does.

verdict: The branch is fit to merge as it is; nothing has to change first. tools/check.sh printed CHECK OK on cbccc58 in my worktree (import; parse 83 scripts, 0 failures; data 0 errors; audio 33 sounds, 1035 checks, 0 failures; tests RESULT: OK; smoke 2 scenes and 5 runs, 0 failures), and the project rules hold: nothing under src/core, tests, docs or wip is touched, one line is added to drive_controller.gd and two to check.sh, the three commit messages end as required, every gain, gap and rate of a sound is in sfx.json or tuning.json, there is no player-facing string, and Audio only reads the snapshot. I reproduced the reports (the three traced legs frame for frame, the Storm's horn 60 frames before each crash and none for a car standing off the lanes with its hazard lights on, six rings of the Call, the Arrival, the example picture read) and measured the real mixer: the engine at 180, 60 and 30 Hz at 160, 40 and 0 km/h with nothing between its harmonics above -136 dB, so no click as the loops turn. Seven findings, none blocking: the first (5 dB off every gain, data only) is best taken with the merge because the cues distort where they matter most, and the second (the Rattle) needs a ruling since the table of 16.5 has no such sound; the other five are small and each has a fix I tried. For the merge itself: the whole diff applies to the tip d8c77a4 with an offset in drive_controller.gd, and in a scratch copy the parse check (86 scripts), the audio check and all 11 smoke runs, the four --boss runs among them, pass there; but at the Checkpoint the siren then chirps every 3 s from the first frame to the verdict at Suspicion 0 (21 chirps a pass with the stand-in bot), which the snapshot's `suspicion_by` on main lets one line of Audio.apply decide once the owner has said what a checkpoint sounds like. Not findings against this branch because they need src/core: DataValidator knows nothing of the synth vocabulary (a broken entry is caught by the boot and by the audio check, not by validate_data), and a snapshot key for the tape deck. Owner's calls the engineer already raised, which I confirm: a yawn turns the horn behind him down by 13 dB (its 370 Hz line fell from -16.3 to -29.3 dB under a long yawn, whose own sweep passes through the horn's two notes), nothing tells him his hazard lights are on, and GDD 17.2 is not met for the tells that have no sound in 16.5. The thirty decisions still have to go into docs/DECISIONS.md. Like the builder and the engineer I heard nothing by ear; every level here is a measurement. My probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/rev4/ and my worktree is left unchanged.
